title: Comparative Sensitivity Analysis of Grid‐Scale Battery Storage Technologies: Feasibility Investigation for Solar Integration in India
abstract: ABSTRACT This study presents a comprehensive techno‐economic and environmental sensitivity analysis of integrating grid‐scale solar photovoltaic systems with multiple energy storage technologies to fulfill state‐level electricity demand in Jharkhand, India—a resource‐rich and coal‐dependent state facing persistent grid reliability challenges. Addressing a critical research gap in sector‐specific, multi‐chemistry storage optimization under dynamic tariff regimes, the study models and compares four storage technologies—lithium ferro phosphate batteries (LFP), sodium‐sulfur batteries (NaS), vanadium redox flow batteries (VRFB), and pumped hydropower storage (PH), each tailored for six‐hour charge retention. The open‐source Solar Alone Multi‐objective Advisor (SAMA) tool, used to model PV‐battery hybrids, has been used with particle swarm optimization. One hundred and twenty‐eight system configurations were simulated across fixed and time‐of‐use tariffs, with and without net metering, under varying inflation (5%–12.5%) and grid price escalation rates (−2.5% to +5%). The analysis rigorously assesses each configuration's payback period, internal rate of return (IRR), return on investment (RoI), levelized cost of energy (LCOE), emissions, and system sizing metrics. The results show that LFP batteries consistently deliver the shortest payback periods (8–13 years), the highest RoI (43%–340%), and the most stable IRR (9%–13%) under all market scenarios, marking them as the most bankable near‐term solution for daily cycling. Pumped hydropower provides moderate payback periods (10–18 years) and achieves highly competitive LCOE values (USD 0.03–0.04 per kWh with net metering), making it ideal for large‐scale, long‐duration storage where suitable sites exist. Sodium‐sulfur batteries reach RoI up to 288% in high‐inflation scenarios but display greater volatility, while vanadium redox flow batteries, with payback periods of 11–22 years and no mid‐life replacements, offer unique advantages for deep‐cycling, stationary industrial applications. Net metering emerges as a dominant policy lever, reducing LCOE from USD 0.06–0.16 per kWh (no export) to USD 0.03–0.04 per kWh (with export) and cutting lifecycle emissions from 0.45 to 0.17 kg/kWh, while enabling a surge in optimal installed PV capacity from 3–5 GW to over 16 GW. The findings accentuate that while LFP offers superior financial performance and rapid capital recovery, sector‐specific technology mapping is essential to maximize grid resilience and renewable integration by deploying NaS and PH for medium and bulk storage, and VRFB for industrial deep cycling. Ultimately, the study provides a replicable, data‐driven framework for selecting and optimizing storage technologies under evolving market structures, supporting Jharkhand's and similar regions' transition from coal reliance to a resilient, renewable‐powered future.
title_zh: Comparative Sensitivity Analysis of Grid‐Scale Battery Storage Technologies: Feasibility Investigation for Solar Integration in India

title: Resolving the LiFePO4 Battery State beyond Voltage-Based Diagnostics Using Surface-Scan MRI
abstract: Abstract Reliable assessment of state of charge (SoC) and state of health (SoH) in commercial batteries remains a major challenge because their closed architecture obscures the underlying electrochemical, structural, and thermal processes, while existing diagnostic methods often provide only indirect, spatially averaged, voltage-based information about battery operation and degradation. Lithium iron phosphate (LFP) is among the most widely deployed cathode materials due to its low cost, long cycle life, and high thermal stability; however, its characteristically flat voltage profile fundamentally limits the information content of conventional diagnostics. In this work, we exploit the large magnetic-susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases and the lithiation-dependent evolution of their phase fractions for accurate and time-efficient determination of SoC in commercial pouch cells and battery packs. Surface-scan magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides new SoC and SoH metrics through quantitative inside-out measurements of battery-induced magnetic field perturbations. LFP is a cathode material particularly well suited to this approach because its biphasic FP/LFP regime spans a large fraction of the usable SoC window while generating substantial magnetic susceptibility contrast between the FP and LFP phases. Under the biphasic approximation, the average magnetic susceptibility follows the lever rule, predicting a linear relationship between the induced magnetic field offset and SoC. Surface-scan MRI experiments confirm this prediction over a broad SoC range. We further establish a framework for spatial mapping of SoC and SoH heterogeneity in multi-cell architectures representative of practical battery packs. Despite minimal voltage differences between cells, the method enables quantitative visualization of charge imbalance and structural heterogeneity on the timescale of seconds.
title_zh: Resolving the LiFePO4 Battery State beyond Voltage-Based Diagnostics Using Surface-Scan MRI

title: Longitudinal proxy pack benchmark generation for remaining useful life assessment of light electric vehicle battery packs in swapping systems
abstract: Abstract Battery swapping enables rapid energy replenishment for light electric vehicles (LEVs), but high-turnover pack circulation requires reliable pack-level health and remaining useful life ( RUL ) assessment. Publicly reusable longitudinal ageing datasets for complete LEV packs remain scarce. We develop a proxy-pack data-generation and learning framework that organizes independently tested cell-ageing records into fixed-member trajectories representing a 48 V-class 16-series configuration. Each trajectory retains 16 physical-cell identities over their common-cycle sequence. Cycle-level member states are aggregated into pack features for predicting a conservative minimum-member proxy RUL, with test barcodes isolated before combinatorial augmentation. Across ten barcode-level splits in each of three source cohorts, same-source tests with endpoints within the augmented training lifetime range achieved a median R² of 0.909 and a median Spearman correlation of 0.997. Tests beyond this range retained strong degradation ordering but showed larger absolute errors. A secondary mixed-source audit of 80 held-out trajectories achieved a median R² of 0.714 and a median Spearman correlation of 0.992. A matched composition-control analysis yielded a median R² by change of -0.015 after balancing barcode reuse and limiting composition overlap, indicating limited sensitivity to training-composition sampling. A complementary physical audit using one fixed 12S3P pack confirmed cell-to-branch-to-pack electrical closure and revealed persistent voltage limitation and migration of the maximum-temperature location. Proxy-pack generation therefore provides a reproducible approach for constructing longitudinal member-aware benchmarks from cell-ageing records and evaluating pack-health and RUL models across varied compositions and lifetime conditions.
title_zh: Longitudinal proxy pack benchmark generation for remaining useful life assessment of light electric vehicle battery packs in swapping systems
